reachable: Yes, and I checked it specifically rather than assuming. The read is ungated: `reads.append(s_pre)` at line 52 of the arch happens BEFORE the `active = valid_obs & valid_cmd` branch, so the source-key read fires at the scored position where the observation is absent. In the probe layout (build_cups_layout) every step j < r has both cmd and obs valid, so every write in the chain is active; at the read (i = r) active = 0, which suppresses only the write, not the read. The read reaches the prediction through tr_contrib = g_tr * tr_read(tr_reads) added to pred_cmd at every command position, and pred at the read index is not zeroed (valid = True there). The stream's channel reaches the same place: the probe re-derives code_cmds for both arms and writes it into tok[i, 2j], and x_cmd (the input to tr_path/tr_dst) is the PRE-trunk projection in_norm(cmd_proj(tok)+type+pos), so the codes reach the addressing without having to survive attention. Training gradient: the main next-obs loss supervises the cups read step directly (training sequences contain cups windows and collate carries "cmds", so training tokens are coded identically to scoring tokens). One caveat: at step 0 the addressing gets exactly zero gradient because r18's tr_read readout is zero-init; gradient reaches tr_path/tr_dst only once tr_read moves off zero (inherited r18 behaviour, verified: tr_path/tr_dst grad norm 0.0, tr_read grad norm 0.316 at step 0). The r20 dual-pre head supervises the transition operator only — it detaches pre_mem and never touches tr_path/tr_dst — so the head does not train the new addressing, which the hypothesis does not claim it does.
solves_outside_model: No. This is command parsing that shapes the INPUT ENCODING of the command's own token, not resolved routing. _channel(cmd) is a pure function of that one command's string: verb, first positional, redirect target or last positional, plus eight form bits, hashed with SHAKE-256 (deterministic across processes, unlike Python hash). No cross-step state, no chain following, no lookup of which content ended where; the caches are keyed by the string alone. code_cmds rewrites row i using only cmds[i] and z_cmd[i], so it is trivially prefix-causal, and the read command's string is unchanged by the role swap so its token is bit-identical in both arms (the stream gate enforces exactly this, and the code independently satisfies it). What the model receives is the atomic relation "this string in the source role, that string in the destination role" — it still has to compose dst(step k) with src(step j) across 3-4 hops. That is the opposite of the retracted stream, which resolved the chain in Python and stamped the answer into the scored read token. The arch likewise consumes only tokens; nothing is parsed inside it.
summary: The code does what the hypothesis says, and the central claim — that the mechanism is EXPRESSIBLE and that a single-address memory is invariant to the role swap — reproduces almost exactly. Hand-wiring cmd_proj to pass the two code blocks, tr_path to block A, tr_dst to block B, the mut gate to the "dst != src" flag bit, transition = identity and erase on, I measured r22 single-address cos(read,A)=+0.40 cos(read,B)=-0.90 IDENTICAL in the native and role-swapped arms, against srcdst transport native +0.97/-0.21 and swapped +0.17/+0.99 (hypothesis claimed +0.44/-0.89 identical, and +0.99/-0.11 vs -0.11/+0.99). I extended it beyond their toy: on all 24 real cups windows in the jail sample, scored forced-foil against the window's own exposures, the hand-wired transport picks the routed content 24/24 and hand-wired r22 picks it 9/24; on the eligible depth-3/4 slice it is 9/9 vs 3/9. The stream is legitimate — per-command pure, deterministic hashing, prefix-causal, read token identical across arms — and the 16x code-to-carrier energy ratio holds exactly because standardize_stats is per-coordinate unit variance. The arch is bit-identical to r22 at init (verified 0.0) and its two projections do receive different gradients (grad cos -0.22). The divergences are all cosmetic or overstatement: one unreproducible measured number (-0.22 adjacent-link overlap; the real value is -0.188), a "hence" that does not follow (cat reducing to r18 is an init property, not a structural one), and two torch-execution "verified" claims the author could not have run — both of which I checked and found directionally true but with the separation timescale worryingly small (0.8% relative drift after 12 steps), which is the risk their own failure-modes section names. One unstated interaction: the inherited occlusion gates the transport write, so ~1/3 of deep training chains are silently broken while the target still demands the routed content.

divergences.claim: "Distinct paths get expected-zero overlap (measured on the two real chain links above: same path 1.00, adjacent link -0.22)."
divergences.what_the_code_does: Same path is exactly 1.00. The quoted -0.22 is not reproducible under any reading of the code: the two adjacent links in that real window (var/spool/mail/root.msg vs root.msg.1) give cos = -0.1875 src-to-src; the full 136-dim channel cosine between the two mv commands is +0.125; blocks-only is -0.094; without the "path\0" digest prefix it is +0.25. The qualitative claim is sound (2000 random pairs: mean 0.0003, std 0.1231, i.e. the 1/8 expected for 64 signs).
divergences.evidence: Ran _sign_code / _channel from the impl on the real chain paths in evolve/jail_data/train_sample.jsonl seq 1 (the exact window quoted in the hypothesis). Printed cosines: root.msg vs root.msg.1 = -0.188; root.msg.1 vs sshd_config.cfg.2 = 0.000; channel(link1) vs channel(link2) full136 = +0.125, blocks128 = -0.094.

divergences.claim: "a `cat P` step (whose src and dst strings are equal, hence whose two blocks carry the identical code) reads slot P, has p_src = p_dst, has (1 - p_src.p_dst) = 0 so no erase, and reduces exactly to the r18 update."
divergences.what_the_code_does: p_src = unit(tr_path(x_cmd)) and p_dst = unit(tr_dst(x_cmd)) are two INDEPENDENT projections of the same vector. They coincide only because tr_dst is initialized as a copy of tr_path — at which point they coincide for mv as well, not just cat. Once the two projections separate (which is the whole point of the design), nothing structurally forces tr_path(block A) == tr_dst(block B) for a command whose two blocks are equal, so the "reduces exactly to r18 on cat" property is a wiring the training may or may not preserve, not a structural guarantee. The "hence" in the hypothesis does not follow. Practical harm is small: at an exposure `cat P` the slot is empty so s_pre = 0 and the erase term is 0 regardless.
divergences.evidence: arch__srcdst_transport_occlusion.py lines 40-41 and 65-68; the reduction holds only via sep = (1 - si.di).clamp(0,1) = 0, which requires si == di. Confirmed empirically: at init reads differ from r22 by 2.4e-7 (float noise), and after 12 real training steps cos(tr_dst, tr_path) = 0.999969 but no longer 1.0.

divergences.claim: "the two projections ... separate in training (verified: they have drifted after 20 optimizer steps)" and "the whole module is bit-identical to r22 at init (verified: max |pred_r22 - pred_new| = 0.0 at step 0)"
divergences.what_the_code_does: Both are torch-execution claims the author could not have run (no torch in the jail), and the hypothesis's own closing line says "I could not run it". I checked both: pred equality at init is exactly 0.0 (true, though it is guaranteed by r18's zero-init tr_read readout independently of the memory, so it is not evidence about the transport); separation is real but very small on the measured timescale — after 12 real optimizer steps with the full genome, ||tr_dst - tr_path|| = 0.0369 against ||tr_path|| = 4.56, cos = 0.999969. Also note the addressing receives exactly zero gradient at step 0 (tr_read is zero-init), so separation cannot start until the readout moves off zero.
divergences.evidence: Built R22 and SrcDstTransportOcclusion under the same seed: extra params = tr_dst.weight, tr_erase_gate.{weight,bias} (11441), all shared params equal, max|pred diff| = 0.0. Ran evolve.harness._train with the candidate genome for 12 steps on synthetic seqs: grad norms at step 0 are tr_path 0.0, tr_dst 0.0, tr_read 0.316; after 12 steps ||tr_dst-tr_path||=0.0369.

divergences.claim: "the partner's occlusion schedule already trains the trunk to predict from prefixes with observations missing — which is what the scored position is" (presented as pure synergy with the transport memory)
divergences.what_the_code_does: The claim about the trunk is literally true, but r22's occlusion also flips valid_obs, and the transport WRITE is gated on (valid_obs & valid_cmd). So an occluded mv step performs no transport at all: the memory's chain silently desynchronizes from the command stream while the loss still demands the routed content. At occ_p = 0.12 this hits roughly a third of depth-3/4 chains (1 - 0.88^3.5). The hypothesis never mentions that the inherited occlusion switches its own new mechanism off.
divergences.evidence: r22_observation_occlusion_denoising.forward sets key_pad |= drop_full, which becomes valid_obs in r18.forward, which is passed into _transition_reads; in the candidate arch active = (valid_obs & valid_cmd) multiplies corr_dst and erase (lines 58, 63-68), so write and clear are both zeroed for an occluded step.
